sourceNote: Gangtok is the capital of Sikkim state at 1437m on a ridge above the Ran River. All records curated from Wikipedia articles and publicly documented sources. Best season Mar–May and Oct–Nov; Jun–Sep is monsoon. Tsomgo Lake (35km) and Nathu La Pass (55km) require Protected Area Permits for non-Sikkim Indians and Restricted Area Permits for foreigners. All records needs_review.

places.name: MG Marg
places.description: Mahatma Gandhi Marg — Gangtok's pedestrianised main promenade, the social spine of the city and consistently rated one of the cleanest streets in India. Lined with shops, restaurants, bakeries, and hotels in low-rise buildings. The street is vehicle-free all day; children play, vendors sell momos and thukpa, and tourists browse craft shops. Evening brings live music from some venues. Free to walk. The bench in front of the Sikkim Tourism office is the classic gathering spot.
places.openingDays: Open all day (pedestrian zone 24hrs; shops approx 09:00–21:00)

places.name: Enchey Monastery
places.description: Nyingma-sect Tibetan Buddhist monastery built 1909 on a hilltop 3km north of Gangtok town, on a site blessed by Lama Druptob Karpo in the 19th century. The monastery is associated with the sacred Tantric dance (Chham) festival held annually in December–January. Houses monks affiliated with the Rumtek Dharma Chakra Centre. Wide views over Gangtok and the Kangchenjunga range from the monastery grounds. Free to enter.

places.name: Do-Drul Chorten Stupa
places.description: One of the most important Buddhist stupas in Sikkim, built 1945 by Trulshik Rinpoche under the direction of Dodrupchen Rinpoche. The white stupa is surrounded by 108 prayer wheels and prayer flags; the internal shrine houses a large mandala. Located near the South Sikkim district boundary 1km from Gangtok town centre. A living religious site; monks and laypeople perform the kora (circumambulation) throughout the day. Free to enter and circumambulate.

places.name: Namgyal Institute of Tibetology
places.description: Foremost research institute for Tibetan and Sikkimese studies, founded 1958 by Chogyal Tashi Namgyal. The library holds over 200 handwritten Buddhist manuscripts on palm leaf and handmade paper, one of the largest collections in the world. The museum displays rare thangkas, ritual objects, masks, and iconography. A Tibetan-style building with painted eaves; a working academic institute open to visitors. Named after the last Chogyal (king) of Sikkim. Free or nominal entry.

places.name: Gangtok Ropeway
places.description: Three-station cable car running from Deorali to Namnang to Tashiling, covering roughly 1km of urban ridge terrain above Gangtok. The ropeway provides aerial views of the city and, on clear days, the Kangchenjunga massif. A government-operated service; timing can be irregular. Entry fee charged. More a scenic overview than a long excursion; popular with families and for photography.
places.openingDays: Daily 09:00–16:00 (check day of; may close for maintenance)

places.name: Tashi Viewpoint
places.description: Viewpoint 8km north of Gangtok on the road towards Phodong, offering one of the clearest panoramas of the Kangchenjunga massif (8586m), Siniolchu (6888m), and the peaks of North Sikkim from a low-altitude vantage point accessible by road. The viewpoint is open early morning for sunrise; best on clear October–November and March–April days. Government-maintained garden with a café. Free entry (small café-area fee may apply). Standard combined with Enchey Monastery on a northern Gangtok loop.

places.name: Banjhakri Falls and Energy Park
places.description: Waterfall in a forested gorge 7km south of Gangtok, packaged within a government eco-park featuring sculptures of the Banjhakri (forest shamanic figure) from Sikkimese folklore. The waterfall drops into a natural pool; the park has walking paths and stone sculptures depicting local mythology. A somewhat commercial setting but the waterfall itself and the Banjhakri mythology make it worthwhile. Entry fee. Combined with Ranka/Lingdum Monastery, 2km further.

places.name: Rumtek Monastery
places.description: Seat of the Kagyu lineage of Tibetan Buddhism and the largest monastery in Sikkim, 23km southwest of Gangtok. The current complex was built 1966 by the 16th Karmapa, who fled Tibet in 1959. The inner shrine houses the Golden Stupa containing the remains of the 16th Karmapa and rare Tibetan artefacts. The monastery complex includes a shedra (monastic college) and several shrines. Access involves a checkpoint; foreigners and Indians require an Inner Line Permit (available at the checkpoint or Gangtok). A living monastic community of the Karma Kagyu order.
places.openingDays: Daily 08:00–18:00 (permit required; checkpoint hours may differ)

places.name: Tsomgo Lake
places.description: Glacial lake at 3753m altitude, 35km east of Gangtok on the Nathu La road. Sacred to the local Buddhist and Hindu communities; the name means 'source of water' in Sikkimese. The lake is frozen Dec–Mar and surrounded by rhododendron forest in spring. Yaks and yak-wool stoles are rented at the lakeside. Protected Area Permit required for Indian nationals (not from Sikkim); Restricted Area Permit for foreigners. Permit available from Gangtok. Full-day excursion from Gangtok; commonly combined with Nathu La Pass.
places.openingDays: Daily 08:00–16:00 (permit required; subject to army/weather closures)

places.name: Nathu La Pass
places.description: Himalayan mountain pass at 4310m on the India-China border, 55km east of Gangtok. One of three open trading border posts between India and China; reopened for bilateral trade in 2006 after being closed since the 1962 war. Indian Army posts are visible at the ridge; the actual border is a fence. The landscape at high altitude — treeless, snow-covered much of the year — is starkly different from Gangtok. Restricted Area Permit mandatory for all visitors (Indian and foreign); permits available from Gangtok in 1 working day. Open Mon, Wed, Thu, Sat, Sun (closed Tue, Fri, and during Chinese national holidays). Full-day excursion; altitude sickness is possible above 4000m.
places.openingDays: Mon, Wed, Thu, Sat, Sun 08:30–14:00 (permit required; closed during military/weather advisories)

places.name: Old Bazaar Gangtok
places.description: The original market street of Gangtok below MG Marg, a living neighbourhood market without tourist packaging. Shops sell Tibetan and Sikkimese handicrafts, dried foods, thankas, incense, and everyday goods. The Old Bazaar operates on foot; the narrow lane is lined with traditional tea shops serving butter tea and thukpa. The produce market in the early morning has vendors from surrounding villages. A grounding counterpart to the polished MG Marg promenade — the Gangtok that residents actually use.

places.name: Tsuk La Khang Royal Chapel
places.description: The Royal Chapel of the Chogyal (King) of Sikkim, located in the former palace grounds near the centre of Gangtok. Built in the traditional Tibetan style with painted murals, bronze statues, and ceremonial objects accumulated over the Chogyal dynasty. A functioning place of worship for the Tibetan Buddhist community. The chapel is open to visitors on the Pang Lhabsol and Losar festivals when special ceremonies are held. Regular visitor access is permitted on certain days. One of the most authentic Tibetan Buddhist cultural sites in Gangtok.
places.openingDays: Open on major Buddhist festivals; limited regular access (confirm locally)
